nahhas-irab:12-12.t: [Translator's note: the entry begins without quoting the verse; the feminine pronoun in فِيهَا refers to الْبِلادِ.] It is on the feminine of the group, as the plural of balad (land); the masculine is also permissible, meaning by it the plural or the singular.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: [Translator's note: the entry does not quote the word; it evidently refers to سَوْطَ.] It may also be read with ṣād (صوط), because ṭāʾ comes after the sīn.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: Among the best things said about it is that it is figurative (majāz), i.e., He watches over (yarṣudu) the deeds of the servants, i.e., nothing escapes Him. Sufyān said: al-mirṣād is the third bridge of Hell.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: فَأَمَّا الْإِنْسانُ إِذا مَا ابْتَلاهُ رَبُّهُ, i.e., tested him, فَأَكْرَمَهُ وَنَعَّمَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَكْرَمَنِ: concerning the meaning of this and what follows there are two views. The first, which is the view of Qatāda, is that when Allah bestows favour on a person and gives him abundance, he says: "My Lord has honoured me with this", and when He straitens his provision, he says: "He has humiliated me". So Allah rebuked man for this and made known to him that giving him abundance is not out of honouring him, nor is straitening him out of humiliating him. Qatāda said: His honouring him is only through his obedience, and His humiliating him is through his disobedience. The other view is that when Allah gives a person abundance he praises Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and when He straitens him he does not praise Him, so Allah rebuked him, because he must praise Him in both states. The rebuke is in His saying: كَلَّا. What indicates the correctness of the first answer is what comes after the verse: بَلْ لا تُكْرِمُونَ الْيَتِيمَ and what follows it, i.e., by this is humiliation, and by its opposite is honour.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: The mafʿūl bihi (direct object) was omitted because the hearer knows it, i.e., "and you do not urge people". Whoever reads تَحَاضُّونَ takes it in the sense of تتحاضّون; one of the two tāʾs was dropped, as in وَلا تَفَرَّقُوا [Āl ʿImrān: 103].

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
The tāʾ (of التراث) is substituted for a wāw (from w-r-th), because it is the closest of the augment letters to it. أَكْلًا is a maṣdar (verbal noun); لَمًّا is its naʿt (adjective).
Al-Farrāʾ said: (لَمًّا means) intense.

nahhas-irab:20-21.t: He said: (جَمًّا means) much. Abū Jaʿfar said: كَلَّا — [Translator's note: the text here reads «تماما في كلّ القرآن قال», apparently corrupt; perhaps "it is a complete stop throughout the Qur'an"] — he said: the meaning is: they ought not to be like this, so desist from this deed. إِذا دُكَّتِ الْأَرْضُ دَكًّا: from Ibn ʿAbbās, i.e., it was shaken; and it (دَكًّا) is an emphatic maṣdar (maṣdar muʾakkid), and likewise the one after it.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: وَجاءَ رَبُّكَ وَالْمَلَكُ صَفًّا: (الملك) means the angels. صَفًّا صَفًّا is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
وَجِيءَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِجَهَنَّمَ: (بجهنم) is in the position of the noun whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent); it is also possible that the noun (the deputy agent) is the maṣdar. يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسانُ: the tāʾ may be assimilated into the dhāl. وَأَنَّى لَهُ الذِّكْرى: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: (الذكرى is) repentance; and it has been said: the meaning is, from what direction will the benefit of the remembrance be his?
يَقُولُ يا لَيْتَنِي: among the Arabs are those who say ليتي, likening it to أنّي. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: قَدَّمْتُ لِحَياتِي, in the Hereafter. Al-Ḥasan said: he knew that there was a life there that has no ending.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t:
This is the reading of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza, and it is the reading by which the proof has been established through consensus. Al-Kisāʾī read فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يُعَذِّبُ عَذابَهُ أَحَدٌ وَلا يُوثِقُ وَثاقَهُ أَحَدٌ [Translator's note: the vowelling printed here is the same as above; al-Kisāʾī's reading is with fatḥa on the dhāl and the thāʾ, i.e., لا يُعَذَّبُ … وَلا يُوثَقُ, passive, as stated below], he said:
And this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, and he argued with two flimsy arguments. One of them is the ḥadīth he claimed from the Prophet ﷺ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The ḥadīth does not have a sound chain (isnād). Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd narrated it to us, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from Abū ʿUbayd, who said: Hushaym [Translator's note: the text reads «هشام»] and ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbbād narrated to us, from Khālid, from Abū Qilāba, from someone whom the Prophet ﷺ taught to recite: فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يُعَذِّبُ عَذابَهُ أَحَدٌ. وَلا يُوثِقُ وَثاقَهُ أَحَدٌ with fatḥa on the dhāl and the thāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar said: And this ḥadīth is clear [Translator's note: presumably "clearly weak"], because if an unknown person (majhūl) occurs in a ḥadīth it is not used as proof outside the Qur'an, so how much less in the Book of Allah, and in opposition to the community (al-jamāʿa) whose reading is from the Prophet?
His other argument is that the Muslims know that no one on the Day of Resurrection punishes except Allah, so how can it be "no one punishes as He punishes"? This is his argument. Abū Jaʿfar said: He overlooked what the scholars said in the interpretation of the verse, for they said — among them al-Ḥasan —: no one in this world punishes with the like of Allah's punishment on the Day of Resurrection. Abū ʿUbayd interpreted the meaning of لا يُعَذِّبُ عَذابَهُ أَحَدٌ as "no one is punished with the punishment of the disbeliever". He was also opposed in this interpretation; among those who opposed him was al-Farrāʾ, who held that the meaning is: no one in this world punishes like the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter. There is a third view on it: that a particular man is meant by it.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t:
It is also permissible to say يا أيّها, because of the vagueness (ibhām) of أيّ. النَّفْسُ is a naʿt (adjective) of أيّ, and الْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ is a naʿt of النفس. If you make it a naʿt of أيّ, its accusative is permissible, because the speech has been completed, just as you say: يا زيد الكريم أقبل ("O Zayd, the noble one, come forward").
And the meaning is: (the soul) at rest in Allah's promise, Mighty and Majestic, and His threat.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t:
ارْجِعِي إِلى رَبِّكِ: concerning its meaning there are two views. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: (return) to your body; so on this view the meaning is that the soul was addressed. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: to Allah; so on this view the address is to the human being, and al-Farrāʾ inclines to this, and to the view that the meaning is that the angels say this to them when they are given their books in their right hands, i.e., return to the reward of your Lord.
فَادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي (29), i.e., among My righteous servants, i.e., be with them. Al-Farrāʾ said:
"Ibn ʿAbbās alone read «فادخلي في عبدي»". Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a mistake — I mean his saying "alone"; this is the reading of Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, Abū Jaʿfar and al-Ḍaḥḥāk. Its analysis in Arabic is in the sense of the genus, i.e., let every spirit enter a servant (body); and it has been said: it is a singular that indicates a plural. The mark of the jussive (jazm) in ادخلي, according to the Kufans, is the dropping of the nūn; the Basrans say: it is not declinable (muʿrab), because it is not an imperfect verb and there is no operator with it to put it in the jussive. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the operator in it is the lām (of command), which is omitted.

nahhas-irab:6-7.t:
أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعادٍ (6): He declined عادا fully (with nunation, ṣarf), making it a name of the tribe-kin (al-ḥayy) [Translator's note: the text reads «للحقّ», evidently a misprint for «للحيّ», "for the clan"]; and the reading of al-Ḍaḥḥāk is بِعادٍ without nunation, making it a name of the tribe (qabīla). In the reading of al-Ḥasan, بِعادٍ إِرَمَ, he put عاد into a genitive construct (iḍāfa) with إِرَمَ and did not decline إرم fully.
This verse is problematic for many of the scholars of Arabic. Many people say that إرم is the name of a place, so how can it be a naʿt (adjective) of عاد or a badal (substitute) for it? And it is asked: how is عاد fully declined while إرم is not? Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī [Translator's note: the text reads «القرطبيّ»] claimed that Iram is Alexandria; al-Maqburī said: Iram is Damascus, and likewise Mālik ibn Anas said: "It has reached me that it is Damascus" — Ibn Wahb narrated this from him. Mujāhid said: Iram is "the ancient one", and something other than this has also been narrated from him. From Ibn ʿAbbās: Iram means "the perished", and from Qatāda: Iram is the tribe.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The discussion of this from the side of Arabic is that the clearest view on it is the statement of Qatāda: Iram is a tribe of ʿĀd. As for Iram being Alexandria or Damascus, that is far-fetched, because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: وَاذْكُرْ أَخا عادٍ إِذْ أَنْذَرَ قَوْمَهُ بِالْأَحْقافِ [al-Aḥqāf: 21]; and al-ḥiqf is sand that has curved and twisted, and neither Damascus nor Alexandria is like that.
It has also been said that إِرَمَ ذاتِ الْعِمادِ is a great city that exists at this time. If this is correct, its summary in grammar is: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعادٍ, the owner of Iram [Translator's note: i.e., with a muḍāf omitted], like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82]. ذاتِ الْعِمادِ is a naʿt of عاد in the sense of the tribe, or of إرم, and likewise.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
In the reading of Ibn al-Zubayr: الَّتِي لَمْ يُخْلَقْ مِثْلُها فِي الْبِلادِ [Translator's note: the text gives the standard wording here, though Ibn al-Zubayr's reading is reported elsewhere as «لم يَخْلُق مثلَها», active voice; the explanation that follows assumes the active], meaning: your Lord did not create the like of ʿĀd in the lands, in the greatness of their bodies and their strength; yet that availed them nothing when they opposed the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so He destroyed them.
«وثمود» is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ), the implied form being "and with Thamūd". It is a diptote (lam yanṣarif) because it is the name of the tribe; whoever declines it fully makes it the name of the clan (al-ḥayy); and whoever puts it in the genitive without nunation dropped the nunation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. «الذين» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective); it may also be in the position of the accusative with the sense of "I mean", or in the position of the nominative with the sense of "they are those who cut out the rock in the valley". جابوا is from the verbs whose third radical is wāw: jāba al-shayʾa yajūbuhu, when he cuts it and goes into it. And the yāʾ was dropped from الواد [Translator's note: the text reads «من الواو», evidently for «من الوادي/الواد»] because it is the end of a verse, and the kasra indicates it.
وَفِرْعَوْنَ is in the position of the genitive, the meaning being "and with Pharaoh"; it is a diptote because it is a foreign (aʿjamī) name. ذِي الْأَوْتادِ is its naʿt. From Ibn ʿAbbās: ذِي الْأَوْتادِ means "possessor of the armies". Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned other than this concerning it, i.e., possessor of many armies who needed to drive tent-pegs on their journeys.
الَّذِينَ طَغَوْا, i.e., they exceeded the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in the lands, i.e., those who were in it.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
[وَالْفَجْرِ is] genitive by the wāw of oath. From Ibn ʿAbbās there are three views on its meaning: among them that it is the dawn of the year, al-Muḥarram; that it is the daytime; and that it is the dawn prayer. As for Masrūq, he said: it is this dawn of yours. He said:
The scholars differed about الفجر: the people of Kufa say it is the whiteness, and the people of Medina say it is the redness. It has been reported from the Arabs: ثوب مشفق and مشفّق, i.e. dyed red.
وَلَيالٍ is conjoined. Its original is ليالي; had it come in its original form, you would say وليالي يا هذا, a diptote, as the poet said: [al-rajaz] 562- قد عجبت منّي ومن يعيليا (She wondered at me and at little Yaʿlā.) They disliked that the weak [final] letter should vary, so the nunation was brought after the yāʾ was dropped, as a compensation for it; it was also said: [a compensation] for the vowel. عَشْرٍ is a naʿt (adjective) of ليال.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
[وَالْوَتْرِ with fatḥa] is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read وَالشَّفْعِ وَالْوِتْرِ [with kasra]. [Translator's note: the source prints the second reading as «وَالْوَتْرِ» with fatḥa; the kasra is supplied according to the discussion.] Abū Jaʿfar said: It is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, who argued from several things, among them that it is the more common in people's usage, and that the ḥadīth transmitters say it so. Abū Jaʿfar said:
If someone were to say "the fatḥa is the more common in people's usage", that would be closer [to the truth], even though he has an argument in both — and [there is no argument] in the saying of the ḥadīth transmitters, because the ḥadīth transmitter does not take care over something like this and does not need to take care over it. [Translator's note: the source's «وإن كان له حجة في كليهما ولا في قول المحدثين» seems defective; perhaps «وإن كان لا حجة في كليهما». Rendered as written.] If someone were to say: the fatḥa is preferable because before it is والشفع, which has a fatḥa, he would have said something resembling the [real] arguments. But they are two good dialect forms, as was read [in transmission] to Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq, who said: I read to Abū ʿUthmān al-Māzinī and Abū Isḥāq al-Ziyādī, from al-Aṣmaʿī, who said: Every single (fard) thing is وتر. The people of the Ḥijāz pronounce الوَتر (odd) with fatḥa and الوِتر (blood-revenge, الذّحل) with kasra; those below them of Qays and Tamīm make them the same. Abū Jaʿfar said: Al-Aṣmaʿī has made clear that they are two dialect forms. In the ḥadīth of ʿUmar and Ibn ʿUmar from the Prophet ﷺ: «الذي تفوته صلاة العصر كأنّما وتر أهله وماله» ("Whoever misses the afternoon prayer, it is as though he had been robbed of his family and his wealth"). It may be derived from الوتر in the sense of blood-revenge (الذحل), so that the meaning is "as though he had been despoiled of his family and wealth", by the merit he lost in missing a prayer. One says وتره يتره وترا وترة when he despoiled him, and the noun is الوتر. It may also be derived from الوتر, i.e. single, so that the meaning is "as though his family and his wealth were diminished", i.e. he was left alone (fard). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ singled out the afternoon prayer for this, as has been said, because it was the time of their occupations and their trading, so attending it was hard for them. And He said: حافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَواتِ وَالصَّلاةِ الْوُسْطى [al-Baqara: 238] — the correct view is that it is the afternoon prayer, and that agrees with the ḥadīth.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: [إِذا يَسْرِ:] the original is يسري. The yāʾ was dropped in writing because it is the end of a verse. Whoever keeps it in continuous recitation brings it according to the original, and drops it at the pause in following the Muṣḥaf, which it is not lawful to contradict. That is good because everything paused on loses its case-ending. Among the good things said about the meaning of يسري is: when it advances as the daytime retreats.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: It was said: [هَلْ فِي ذلِكَ قَسَمٌ لِذِي حِجْرٍ means] "is there [in that] something sufficient?". Among the good things said about it is that the meaning is: Is there in that something by which people of reason swear, magnifying what is sworn by and reinforcing what is sworn to? [Translator's note: the source has «يقسم به … لما أقيم به»; «أقيم» is read as «أقسم», and likewise «يقيمون» below as «يقسمون».] Some scholars inferred from this, and from His magnifying it, that the meaning is "by the Lord of the dawn", because people of reason and faith swear only by Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade anyone to say "by the Kaʿba"; rather, [one should swear] by Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He [Translator's note: the source's «بل خبر عن الله» is unclear; rendered according to the evident sense.], as ʿUmar and Ibn ʿUmar related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: «Allah forbids you to swear by your fathers; whoever swears, let him swear by Allah or keep silent.» ʿUmar said: So I have not sworn by it since, neither speaking for myself (ذاكرا) nor relating it from another (آثرا). In another ḥadīth: «Whoever swears by other than Allah has associated partners [with Him] (أشرك)», and in another: «has disbelieved (كفر)». Abū Jaʿfar said: His saying فما حلفت بها is an allusion to the oath (اليمين), which had not been mentioned before, because the hearer knows it. His saying ذاكرا means "saying [it]", as one says ذكر لي فلان كذا ("so-and-so told me such-and-such"), and ولا آثرا means "nor reporting [it]". The meaning of «Whoever swears by other than Allah has associated partners» is: he has done the deed of the polytheists, and likewise "has disbelieved". That is one view. It was also said: فقد أشرك means he has made a partner for Allah in magnification. It was also said: the meaning of «فقد كفر» is "he has covered and concealed the command of Allah", because He commanded that one swear only by Allah.
